Subject: Dedicated GPU sizing for Wavefront AI pilot

Hi Marissa,

We're kicking off a 6-week pilot at Wavefront to evaluate a dedicated serving tier for our real-time QA product. High level: ~25 sustained user-facing inference requests/sec during business hours, with spikes up to ~220 rps in short bursts. Each user request currently triggers 2 model calls (context + answer).

Quick stats we have now:
- Avg prompt length: ~120 tokens
- Avg response length: ~350 tokens
- Typical session: 3–5 exchanges, session TTL ~45s before idle
- KV reuse expected when users stay in-session; majority (~70%) are multi-turn
- SLO target: p95 < 150ms, p99 < 350ms for the main (answer) call
- We expect pilot traffic to be concentrated in US-east; budget prefers a small reserved pool (1–3 GPUs) if possible during pilot.

Can you send a short sizing checklist or a template we can fill? Also attaching a small telemetry dump from our staging cluster to help (wavefront-telemetry-sample.csv).

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min tech check if useful.

Samir

Thanks for the telemetry, Samir — this is exactly the level of detail we want for an initial sizing pass. I've dropped a compact questionnaire below that captures the inputs our pre-sales sizing engine needs. If you can fill the bullets (or attach a short doc), we'll run a first-pass capacity sketch and follow with a 30-min runbook sync.

Redwood pre-sales sizing checklist (short):
- Peak burst rps and typical sustained rps (specify 1m/5m/15m averages)
- Breakdown: % of single-turn vs multi-turn sessions; avg exchanges per session
- Prompt distribution: % short (<50 tokens) | medium (50–250) | long (>250)
- Response distribution: mean and 90/99 percentiles in tokens
- Concurrent sessions target and expected session TTL distribution (50th/95th)
- Target SLOs per route (p50/p95/p99 latency targets) and whether streaming is required
- Acceptable quantization / model-variant tolerance (e.g., 4-bit ok vs need fp16)
- KV cache reuse expectations (per-session affinity, reuse %), and whether state is sticky to a user
- Failure/fallback rules (serve smaller model at higher latency vs queue)
- Any compliance/region constraints (VPC/on-prem preference)

I also attached our lightweight sizing template to collect the same data: redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx. Once we have the completed sheet + sample telemetry, I'll run a draft footprint and share a short note with recommended GPU mix and a 90/95% confidence capacity range.

Propose a 30-min tech check next Tue 4/27 at 10am PT — OK for you?

Best,
Marissa Cole

Samir / team — a few technical clarifications from the runtime side that materially change GPU mixing and batch sizing:

1) Concurrency distribution: can you share a 24-hr histogram of concurrent in-flight model calls (not just rps)? We usually bucket by 1/5/15/60s windows; tail occupancy shapes batch latency.

2) Session affinity & KV reuse: if sessions are sticky and KV reuse is high, effective per-token cost drops a lot. Please indicate: average KV reuse (requests that hit existing cache) and percent of cold-start prompts.

3) Prompt/response variance: your averages are helpful, but P90/P99 token lengths are critical. A small fraction of 2x–3x longer responses can double memory pressure on some GPUs. If possible, include token percentiles in the CSV.

4) Warm vs burst routing: do you need guaranteed p99 for bursts, or is graceful degradation acceptable (e.g., failover to smaller model or queued retries)? That determines whether we size for headroom or use canary fallback policies.

5) Model compatibility & quantization: which model family and size are you evaluating in pilot? Some families react poorly to aggressive quantization; that impacts whether we recommend higher-memory SKUs vs more GPU count.

If you prefer, we can take the CSV and produce a short note with two sizing options: a conservative reserved pool (opt for p99 headroom) and an economical pooled mode (accept fallbacks, reduce GPU memory footprint).

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
